headline: End of an era: Lionel Messi retires from Argentina national team
summary: The legendary captain, who led Argentina to World Cup and Copa América glory, says he has nothing left to give the country.
details: Lionel Messi has officially announced his retirement from the Argentina national team, marking the end of a two-decade long journey with the iconic number 10 jersey.
Messi stated that the decision was painful for his soul, but he believes he has nothing left to give to the national side after achieving every major milestone.
His career with Argentina was marked by early struggles and criticism, where he was often compared to Maradona and questioned for not winning major trophies for his country.
After years of heartbreak, including losses in the 2014 World Cup and 2015-2016 Copa América finals, Messi finally broke the drought in 2021 by winning the Copa América.
The pinnacle of his career came in 2022, when he led Argentina to a dramatic World Cup victory, ending a 36-year wait for the nation and silencing all critics.
Following his World Cup success, he added another Copa América title in 2024, ensuring his legacy as the most successful captain in Argentina's history.
Messi's journey is celebrated not just for the trophies, but for his resilience in the resilience in the coming back from retirement in 2018 after multiple failures.
The football world now bids farewell to a man who transformed the game and became the symbol of a nation's dreams and love for the football.
caption:
The number 10 is stepping down. Lionel Messi has retired from the Argentina national team.

Lionel Messi has officially announced his retirement from the Argentina national team, marking the end of a two-decade long journey with the iconic number 10 jersey.

Messi stated that the decision was painful for his soul, but he believes he has nothing left to give to the national side after achieving every major milestone.

His career with Argentina was marked by early struggles and criticism, where he was often compared to Maradona and questioned for not winning major trophies for his country.

After years of heartbreak, including losses in the 2014 World Cup and 2015-2016 Copa América finals, Messi finally broke the drought in 2021 by winning the Copa América.

The pinnacle of his career came in 2022, when he led Argentina to a dramatic World Cup victory, ending a 36-year wait for the nation and silencing all critics.

Following his World Cup success, he added another Copa América title in 2024, ensuring his legacy as the most successful captain in Argentina's history.

Messi's journey is celebrated not just for the trophies, but for his resilience in the resilience in the coming back from retirement in 2018 after multiple failures.

The football world now bids farewell to a man who transformed the game and became the symbol of a nation's dreams and love for the football.

headline: Cabinet approves ninth pay scale for government employees
summary: The new salary structure will be implemented in three phases, with pensions increasing by 55% to 100%.
details: The Bangladesh Cabinet has officially approved the proposal for the ninth pay scale for government officials and employees.
Under the new structure, basic salaries will be implemented in three distinct phases to manage the fiscal impact.
Pensioners will see a significant increase, with pension amounts rising between 55% and 100% across five different stages.
While basic pay increases are being rolled out, additional allowances will be introduced starting in 2028.
The move aims to adjust the compensation of government workers to reflect current economic conditions and inflation.
